problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=x(t)+4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=4,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[-2,\text{ }1]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[0,\text{ }1]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options below regarding the given system.$\,$
$y=-\frac{1}{2}x$ is {{field-1}} line.

$\,$
{{field-2}} is {{field-3}} line.

$\,$
The equilibrium point (origin) is {{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

- The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=-\frac{1}{2}x.
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line and approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$ So, $y=-\frac{1}{2}x$ is $\text{an unstable}$ line.

- The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
x=0.
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line and approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$ So, $x=0$ is $\text{an unstable}$ line.

Therefore, the equilibrium point (origin) is $\text{an unstable node (source)}.$ 

**Note:** The phase portrait of the system looks as follows:
